title: Reseat a dropped bicycle chain
instruction: Guide the dropped chain sideways onto the chainring, then turn the crank to check that the chain drives the rear sprocket.
context: A dropped bicycle chain can be restored by guiding its upper run back into the tooth plane while turning the crank.
setup: A bench-scale bicycle drivetrain with 26 front teeth, 16 rear teeth, a crank and pedal, and a loose upper chain run starting 28 mm outboard of its target plane.
scoring: 0.5 once lateral travel exceeds 21 mm towards the tooth plane. Full credit once the engaged upper run has settled by more than 5 mm and the rear sprocket rotates over 1.40 rad.
reset_notes: Shift the upper chain run outboard and reset crank angle, sprocket angle and the engagement state.
fidelity: The visible chain is a continuous moving loop. Contact still uses a guided upper-run proxy. Engaged rotation transfers load through a compliant 26:16 coupling with backlash. The script verifies a partial turn and does not model tooth-by-tooth chain contact.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.00 in 1,200 steps. Scripted dual-YAM demo: 1.00 in 401 steps.
